Beta_actin.reason: Cytoskeletal housekeeping protein. Present in every cell; the registry already records its use as 'housekeeping'.

CD107a.reason: LAMP1, a lysosomal membrane protein present in all nucleated cells.

CD11b.reason: Myeloid integrin. Informative in principle; excluded by the registry, and carried as a marker-dropout arm rather than a panel member.

CD38.reason: Plasma cells and activated lymphocytes, plus some endothelium. Batch-1 panel only.

CD39.reason: ENTPD1. Tregs, B-cell subsets and endothelium; not broadly expressed.

CD44.reason: Broadly expressed across immune, epithelial and mesenchymal compartments.

CD57.reason: NK cells and terminally differentiated cytotoxic T cells.

CD99.reason: Broadly expressed. Also has no DCT vocabulary entry.

Caveolin.reason: Caveolae scaffolding protein, enriched in endothelium -- the registry itself types it Endothelial. It has the HIGHEST label-free Gini of any marker in the panel (0.753). Previously mislabelled uninformative here for the wrong reason: it has no DCT vocabulary entry, which is a different fact and is now recorded separately.

Collagen_IV.reason: Basement-membrane ECM. It labels MATRIX, not cells: a per-cell mean reports adjacency to a basement membrane, not the cell's identity.

DAPI.reason: Nuclear counterstain -- dsDNA IS in the vocabulary. Withheld by a crosswalk decision and carried as the with_dapi arm, not here.

Granzyme_B.reason: Cytotoxic granule protein: CD8 T and NK. Absent from every other compartment.

HLA_A.reason: MHC class I. Near-universal on nucleated cells; level varies but presence does not separate compartments.

HLA_DR.reason: MHC class II. Constitutive on B cells, dendritic cells and macrophages; inducible on activated T cells; largely absent from resting exocrine epithelium and stroma. One of the strongest non-lineage discriminators here.

IAPP.reason: Failed marker throughout this project; excluded by the registry.

ICOS.reason: Activated T cells, notably Tregs; T-lineage restricted.

IDO1.reason: Dendritic cells and macrophages, and some epithelium under interferon. Partial, not universal -- which is what makes it discriminative.

Ki67.reason: Proliferation. Orthogonal to identity by construction -- any compartment can cycle.

LAG3.reason: T-cell restricted, same argument as PD-1.

M2Gal3.reason: Galectin-3 / Mac-2, a macrophage marker. Informative in principle; the model cannot see it because there is no vocabulary entry.

PCNA.reason: Proliferation, orthogonal to identity. Also has no vocabulary entry.

PD_1.reason: T-cell restricted in this tissue, so its presence is lymphocyte evidence regardless of what its level means functionally.

PD_L1.reason: Myeloid and interferon-exposed epithelium. Partial rather than universal.

SOX2.reason: Neural/stem transcription factor with no expected pancreatic resident population; carries no compartment signal in this tissue.

TCF_1.reason: TCF7. Naive/memory T cells; T-lineage restricted.

TOX.reason: T-cell restricted transcription factor; nuclear, so spatially crisp.

VISTA.reason: Broad myeloid/lymphoid checkpoint. Also has no DCT vocabulary entry.

iNOS.reason: Activated myeloid cells. Myeloid-restricted in this tissue.

fields.in_dct_vocabulary: Can the model see it at all? A crosswalk fact, independent of the above.
fields.lineage_informative: Does exclusivity of this marker carry compartment information? Biology only.

gini_caveat: The cross-check is DESCRIPTIVE, not decisive, and the data says so: genuine lineage markers span the range (Caveolin 0.753 down to TP63 0.134, FOXP3 0.202, CD4 0.203), because a low Gini can mean 'rare or weakly stained' as easily as 'on everything'. So a high Gini is neither necessary nor sufficient for compartment information. ICOS, Granzyme_B and TOX are declared informative and sit low; that disagreement is reported and left standing, not reconciled.
how_decided: Declared from known expression biology, per marker, in writing, so a reader who has never seen the model's output can check it. NOT fitted to the gate and not derived from any model output. Cross-checked independently against a label-free dispersion statistic computed from this run's own expression parquet -- see marker_exclusivity_gini.json -- and disagreements are reported, not reconciled. CORRECTED 2026-08-24 after the Gini cross-check: the first draft collapsed 'carries no compartment information' and 'has no DCT vocabulary entry' into one flag, which mislabelled Caveolin -- an endothelial marker the registry itself types Endothelial, and the highest-Gini marker in the panel. The two are now separate fields. The cross-check catching this is the reason it exists.
not_a_threshold: This file selects which channels are handed to the model. It derives no cutoff, calls no marker positive, and asserts no expected frequency for any cell type.
question: Which non-lineage markers carry compartment information by EXCLUSIVITY -- expressed on some compartments and not others -- and which are present on everything and so add a channel token without adding evidence?
why: The type/state split from marker_registry.json is too crude to choose a panel subset with. The registry declines to assign state markers a broad_compartment at all (every one is uses=['deferred_state'], broad_compartment=null), and its mutually_exclusive and families fields are empty, so nothing pre-existing answers this.
